adequacy_rule: Coverage is reported with its 95% Wilson interval over replicates, and the standard-error ratio (the mean standard error over the empirical standard deviation of the estimate) with a 95% percentile interval from resampling replicates. Labels are applied in this order: a method is anti-conservative for a contrast and scenario if the upper end of its coverage interval is below 0.925, the liberal criterion of Bradley (1978) for a nominal 95% interval; conservative if the lower end is above 0.975; adequate if its estimated coverage is at least 0.925 and its standard-error ratio is at least 0.9; otherwise inconclusive.

adequacy_rule_history.wording: A method is adequate for a contrast and scenario if the upper end of the 95% Monte Carlo interval of its coverage reaches 0.925 and the mean of its standard errors is at least 0.9 times the empirical standard deviation of the estimate; anti-conservative if that upper end is below 0.925; otherwise inconclusive.
adequacy_rule_history.replaced: because at 50 replicates it would accept coverage near 0.86

adequacy_rule_history.wording: A method is adequate for a contrast and scenario if its estimated coverage is at least 0.925, the liberal criterion of Bradley (1978) for a nominal 95% interval, at most 0.975, and the mean of its standard errors is at least 0.9 times the empirical standard deviation of the estimate; conservative if its coverage exceeds 0.975 and its standard errors meet the same bound; anti-conservative if the upper end of the 95% Monte Carlo interval of its coverage is below 0.925; otherwise inconclusive.
adequacy_rule_history.replaced: because its labels for adequate and conservative rest on point estimates, which at 50 replicates label a correctly calibrated interval adequate only about half the time
